neighbours.label: anxious suspense: waiting for an uncertain, possibly bad outcome (agonised waiting for news, nail-biting anticipation)
fire: Her parents paced the hospital corridor, waiting for the surgeon to come out.
Hours passed with no word from the rescue team searching the collapsed mine.
The whole town held its breath as the final votes were counted.
He refreshed his inbox every minute, dreading the result of the biopsy.
The crew's families sat by the radio, praying for any sign of the lost boat.
With seconds left on the clock and the score tied, nobody in the stadium could breathe.
She stared at the phone all night, terrified it would ring with bad news.
We waited in agonising silence for the jury to return its verdict.
quiet: Her parents walked out of the hospital, relieved that the surgery had gone well.
The rescue team returned home after a routine training day at the mine.
The whole town gathered in the square to celebrate the election winner.
He opened his inbox and read a cheerful note from his sister.
The crew's families sat on the dock, eating lunch in the sunshine.
The stadium emptied slowly after the comfortable home win.
She chatted on the phone all evening with an old school friend.
We listened politely as the judge described the court's new schedule.

notes: Card top examples: waiting in vain for news, agony of those watching for a missing ship; output promotes anxiety/tension/suspense/dread. Probe: anxious waiting 0.58, calm queueing 0.30, so near misses are calm, resolved situations rather than calm waiting.
